_comment: Hand-written bookkeeping for docs/FORK.md. scripts/fork-pr-table.sh merges this with the live GitHub API data; the rendered tables live between the markers in docs/FORK.md. Every open PR that is missing a note here gets a loud TODO row, so nothing is ever silently omitted. A note is the short form, shown wherever the pull request appears: "detail" is the long form, written in the ledger of docs/FORK.md and left off the front page, and "wip" marks a pull request whose branch is still being reworked here.

front_claim_sentence: Everything general enough is submitted upstream, which means

2441.note: Save, decode and branch latents for Wan, LongCat, LTX-2, MiniMax H3, Magi Human and Ovi; pick a latent file straight from a video. Upstream has rewritten 14 of its 26 files since it branched, four of them no longer merge, and the splice into the MiniMax H3 transformer still merges quietly into the 58 lines upstream deleted there

2292.note: A default output filename for every model, with a template checked before the generation starts

2290.short: the keywords, the format specs, the precheck
2290.note: Effective-output keywords and Python format specs for the Output Filename box

2535.note: DLSS temporal upscaling at x3-x4, up to x6 on RTX 50, with the native Linux Frame Generation worker and installer

2295.note: Native Linux DLSS Frame Generation worker, temporal-only x2-x4 (x5/x6 on RTX 50)

2284.note: SpargeAttn builds from source on Linux with CUDA 13 for the Python versions the prebuilt cp311 wheel does not cover; upstream wheel stays

2286.note: scripts/install-flashattn.sh, a Linux builder for flash-attn 2.8.3.post1 on RTX 50xx (Blackwell)

2289.note: Optional Sol-Attn sparse self-attention for native LTX-2 inference (experimental)

2551.note: Keep LTX-2 on CUDA Graph and stop the minutes-long first steps of PyTorch compilation; the Inductor cache of a session is kept and its shapes capped. The copy in this fork carries the measured RTX 5090 timings in docs/MODELS.md; its code lines are identical

2553.note: Prompt enhancement keeps loading when Auto cannot size the drafter: where WanGP cannot read the drafter, Auto decides on the model's own size instead of the prompt enhancer failing to start

2568.note: Time stamps at the start of the console lines WanGP prints, on the lines the terminal draws only
2568.detail: Lines are stamped with real, local, millisecond time, and the lines of an inference are stamped and logged in order at the moment they are written, so the console says what WanGP is doing and when. Each console stream now owns its buffer and is written out as one indivisible block: a line is no longer broken mid-row, no longer loses its carriage returns, and no longer leaves its cursor, colour and progress bar on the screen after WanGP quits.

2288.note: Sliding Window sizes up to 999 frames for every video model

2482.note: Crash when saving audio that came out empty
2482.detail: Saving audio that came out empty no longer crashes the save, so a job that ends up with no audio keeps its video.

2478.note: “Continue Video” audio joins when the soundtrack ends early
2478.detail: Continuing a video no longer stops when its soundtrack ends a little before the last frame: WanGP asks the model for no more of that closing audio than the frames it can regenerate, and keeps the source audio up to where it ends, so the joins between sliding windows keep their timing.

2526.note: Shell prompt left dead after Ctrl+C in a WanGP run
2526.detail: WanGP takes the terminal as it finds it and returns it in that state: at the end of a run, on Ctrl+C, on *Save and Quit* and on *Restart*, on Windows as well, and it repairs a terminal that arrives broken. The ffmpeg and TTS helper programs read the keyboard on the terminal they share with the shell and turn echo, line editing and Ctrl+C off, so a run that ends on one of them leaves the shell prompt dead with `reset` the only way back. A `--console-guard` option leaves the terminal alone for a setup that owns the terminal already; it defaults to on.

2565.note: SyntaxWarning printed at startup by the About tab credits line

2600.note: Audio Guidance setting ignored by Ovi generations, which ran at a fixed 4.0

2639.note: Video continuation task with an empty Source Video dividing the frame count by zero after the model loaded, instead of asking for the file

2640.note: ffmpeg, ffprobe and the other helper programs WanGP starts are given no keyboard and a process group of their own, so a program that reads the keyboard cannot leave the shell prompt dead

closed_reason.2286: not picked up; the builder script stays in this fork

addressed_upstream_comment: Pull requests closed because upstream wrote the same fix itself, and never merged mine. They stay on the front page's table with that state, since the fork no longer needs them: 'note' is the reason the ledger gives, 'addressed_upstream_commit' names upstream's own commit, whose WanGP release the generator reads from wgp.py at that commit rather than typing it here, and 'addressed_upstream_when' places the rare case where upstream wrote the fix inside a larger change of its own and no commit carries it alone.

addressed_upstream.2600: the fix is upstream's own: it renames audio_cfg_scalecale to audio_cfg_scale in the same three lines of models/wan/ovi_fusion_engine.py, so the Audio Guidance setting reaches Ovi
addressed_upstream.2482: the fix is upstream's own: it normalises an empty track in _prepare_audio_array to the frame-first shape this pull request gave it in write_wav_file, which leaves the guard added here unreachable
addressed_upstream.2565: the fix is upstream's own: the credits line was rewritten with the escape as part of a larger update

fork_only.note: Local fixes around the DLSS entries: the Frame Generation multipliers offered on a multi-GPU host, and a saved Frame Generation choice that the menus used to reset (part of #2535)
